claim: ntfy is a simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service that sends notifications to phone or desktop via PUT/POST without signup or fees, written mainly in Go, with ~30.7k GitHub stars.
quote: ntfy is a simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. It allows you to send notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts from any computer, without having to sign up or pay any fees.

claim: ntfy lets you publish to named topics over HTTP PUT/POST and subscribe via its own open-source Android/iOS apps or the web; it can also act as a UnifiedPush distributor.
quote: ntfy.sh | Push notifications to your phone or desktop via PUT/POST

claim: ntfy implements UnifiedPush, enabling push notifications without Google Firebase Cloud Messaging, acting as a distributor for UnifiedPush-compatible apps like Element and FluffyChat.
quote: ntfy implements UnifiedPush, the standard which makes it possible to send and receive push notifications without using Google's Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) service.

claim: Gotify is a simple self-hosted server for sending (REST API) and receiving (WebSocket) messages in real-time, with a web UI, its own Android app, and CLI; written in Go with ~15.1k GitHub stars.
quote: A simple server for sending and receiving messages in real-time per WebSocket. (Includes a sleek web-ui)

claim: Gotify's Android app subscribes to the server's WebSocket message stream and creates push notifications on newly received messages, running independently of cloud push services.
quote: subscribing/receiving messages via a web socket connection

claim: Apprise is a notification routing library and CLI that dispatches one message to almost all popular notification services via a common syntax; it lists Gotify, Pushover, Telegram, Discord, Slack and others as targets, with ~16.7k GitHub stars.
quote: Apprise allows you to send a notification to almost all of the most popular notification services available to us today such as: Telegram, Discord, Slack, Amazon SNS, Gotify, etc.

claim: Apprise-API is a lightweight REST microservice wrapping the Apprise library, acting as a gateway that fans out one HTTP request to 130+ downstream services via stateless or stateful (stored config key) modes.
quote: A lightweight REST framework that wraps the Apprise Notification Library ... send notifications to more than 130+ services ... an incredibly lightweight gateway to Apprise
